statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(words) such that words[i] is a subsequence of s. Here words[i] is a subsequence of s iff there exist indices 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{len(words[i])-1} < len(s) with s[j_k] = words[i][k] for every k with 0 <= k < len(words[i]). Duplicate entries in words are counted once per index.
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(s) <= 50000, len(words) >= 1, len(words) <= 5000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), 1 <= len(words[i]) <= 50; every byte of s and of every words[i] is between 97 and 122 inclusive.

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result r; it does not fail. In particular, no arithmetic overflow occurs, because the returned count is at most len(words) <= 5000.
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(s) <= 50000, len(words) >= 1, len(words) <= 5000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), 1 <= len(words[i]) <= 50; every byte of s and of every words[i] is between 97 and 122 inclusive.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= len(words).
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(s) <= 50000, len(words) >= 1, len(words) <= 5000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), 1 <= len(words[i]) <= 50; every byte of s and of every words[i] is between 97 and 122 inclusive.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is at most the number of indices i with 0 <= i < len(words) and len(words[i]) <= len(s).
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(s) <= 50000, len(words) >= 1, len(words) <= 5000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), 1 <= len(words[i]) <= 50; every byte of s and of every words[i] is between 97 and 122 inclusive.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = len(words) if and only if for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), words[i] is a subsequence of s. Subsequence means there exist indices 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{len(words[i])-1} < len(s) with s[j_k] = words[i][k] for every k with 0 <= k < len(words[i]).
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(s) <= 50000, len(words) >= 1, len(words) <= 5000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), 1 <= len(words[i]) <= 50; every byte of s and of every words[i] is between 97 and 122 inclusive.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if there is no index i with 0 <= i < len(words) such that words[i] is a subsequence of s. Subsequence means there exist indices 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{len(words[i])-1} < len(s) with s[j_k] = words[i][k] for every k with 0 <= k < len(words[i]).
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(s) <= 50000, len(words) >= 1, len(words) <= 5000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), 1 <= len(words[i]) <= 50; every byte of s and of every words[i] is between 97 and 122 inclusive.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r > 0, there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(words) and indices 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{len(words[i])-1} < len(s) such that s[j_k] = words[i][k] for every k with 0 <= k < len(words[i]).
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(s) <= 50000, len(words) >= 1, len(words) <= 5000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), 1 <= len(words[i]) <= 50; every byte of s and of every words[i] is between 97 and 122 inclusive.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r with r < len(words), there exists an index i with 0 <= i < len(words) such that words[i] is not a subsequence of s. Here words[i] is not a subsequence of s means there are no indices 0 <= j_0 < ... < j_{len(words[i])-1} < len(s) with s[j_k] = words[i][k] for every k with 0 <= k < len(words[i]).
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(s) <= 50000, len(words) >= 1, len(words) <= 5000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), 1 <= len(words[i]) <= 50; every byte of s and of every words[i] is between 97 and 122 inclusive.

statement: Whenever the function returns r for (s, words) and r' for (s, words'), we have r = r'.
preconditions: s and words satisfy: len(s) >= 1, len(s) <= 50000, len(words) >= 1, len(words) <= 5000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), 1 <= len(words[i]) <= 50; every byte of s and of every words[i] is between 97 and 122 inclusive. The list words' also satisfies the same length and byte constraints, and words' is a permutation of words: len(words') = len(words) and there is a bijection p on {0,...,len(words)-1} with words'[i] = words[p(i)] for every i.

statement: Whenever the function returns r for (s, words) and r' for (s, words'), if for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), words[i] is a subsequence of s if and only if words'[i] is a subsequence of s, then r = r'. Subsequence is defined by the existence of strictly increasing matching indices in s.
preconditions: s, words, and words' all satisfy: len(s) >= 1, len(s) <= 50000, len(words) >= 1, len(words) <= 5000, len(words') >= 1, len(words') <= 5000, and all their word lengths are between 1 and 50; every byte of s and of every words[i] and words'[i] is between 97 and 122 inclusive. Also len(words') = len(words).

statement: Whenever the function returns r for (s, words) and r' for (s, words'), if words[i] is a subsequence of s then r = r' + 1, and otherwise r = r'. Subsequence is defined by the existence of strictly increasing matching indices in s.
preconditions: s and words satisfy len(s) >= 1, len(s) <= 50000, len(words) >= 2, len(words) <= 5000, and every word length is between 1 and 50; every byte of s and of every words[i] is between 97 and 122 inclusive. Also 0 <= i < len(words), and words' is obtained from words by deleting index i: len(words') = len(words) - 1, words'[j] = words[j] for j < i, and words'[j] = words[j+1] for j >= i.

statement: Whenever the function returns r for (s, words), r1 for (s, words1), and r2 for (s, words2), we have r = r1 + r2.
preconditions: s, words1, and words2 all satisfy the input constraints: len(s) >= 1, len(s) <= 50000, len(words1) >= 1, len(words1) <= 5000, len(words2) >= 1, len(words2) <= 5000, all word lengths are between 1 and 50, and all bytes are between 97 and 122 inclusive. Also words is the concatenation words1 ++ words2.

statement: Whenever the function returns r for (s, words) and r' for (s', words), we have r <= r'. (Equivalently: every word that is a subsequence of s is also a subsequence of s', by transitivity of the subsequence relation.)
preconditions: s and s' with 1 <= len(s) <= 50000, 1 <= len(s') <= 50000 and all bytes of s and s' between 97 and 122; words with 1 <= len(words) <= 5000, 1 <= len(words[i]) <= 50 and all bytes between 97 and 122; and s is a subsequence of s', i.e. there are 0 <= k_0 < ... < k_{len(s)-1} < len(s') with s'[k_t] = s[t] for all 0 <= t < len(s).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), if some byte b with 97 <= b <= 122 occurs in words[i] but does not occur in s (there is no j with 0 <= j < len(s) and s[j] = b), then words[i] is not a subsequence of s; consequently r is at most the number of indices i such that every byte of words[i] occurs in s.
preconditions: len(s) >= 1, len(s) <= 50000, len(words) >= 1, len(words) <= 5000, and for every i with 0 <= i < len(words), 1 <= len(words[i]) <= 50; every byte of s and of every words[i] is between 97 and 122 inclusive.
